reason: The outgoing motor fibers need insulation, and the support cells have membrane sheets that appear suited to wrap them.
expectation: The support cells will insulate the motor neuron fibers.

effect: The insulated fibers formed motor nerves, and the next goal is to guide a reach using sight and muscle commands.
reaction: The segmented wrapping and gaps made the role of the support cells clearer.
reason: The seeing control system needs a visible target to guide the reach.
expectation: The system will register the target's position for the reach.

effect: The control system has registered the target's location, so it can now help guide the arm.
reaction: The sensory arrows make the path from the target to the brain clear.
reason: The motor nerves need to connect to the arm's muscles to carry movement commands.
expectation: The motor nerves will connect the control pathway to the arm's muscles.

effect: The motor nerves now connect to the arm muscles, leaving the target-aware control system to direct the reach.
reaction: The branching nerves make the connection to the muscles clear.
reason: The control system has the target location, and the nerve-linked arm can receive movement commands.
expectation: The control system will send commands through the nerves to guide the arm toward the target.

effect: The arm can now reach toward the seen target; the next goal is to add information from the arm itself.
reaction: The separate visual and motor pathways made their roles in the reach clear.
reason: The stretch receptors sit among muscle fibers and send signals back, so they seem suited to provide information from the arm.
expectation: The receptors and sensory nerves will add feedback about muscle stretch to the reaching arm.

effect: The arm now has feedback from muscle sensors, and the chapter is complete. The result distinguishes sensing the arm’s position from locating a target.
reaction: The eyes-closed example made that distinction clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the stretch receptors was most worthwhile because it connected muscle sensors to position feedback and showed what that feedback can and cannot tell you.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the motor nerves to the arm was a predictable intermediate step; its picture showed the connection, but added less explanation than the completed reach.

surprise.text: The distinction between knowing where the arm is with eyes closed and locating an unseen target sharpened my understanding of position feedback.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the item titles and pictures gave a practical reason for each connection.

continue.text: I would continue to see how these pathways connect to other body systems. The completed reach brought the separate sensory and motor pieces together clearly.
